name: Eperisone
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Eperisone is a centrally acting muscle relaxant with a short half-life (about 1.7 hours). The Japanese package insert contains no kidney-impairment guidance or kidney pharmacokinetic data; it advises dose reduction and caution in older adults. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The Japanese package insert does not address kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 150 mg/day in 3 divided doses after meals (50 mg three times daily), adjusted for age and symptoms (PMDA insert).
The Japanese package insert gives no kidney dosing or kidney pharmacokinetic data. Use with caution and specialist judgment.

monitoring: Weakness, unsteadiness, drowsiness (reduce dose or stop; no driving). Shock, anaphylaxis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis: stop at once. Liver function (may worsen hepatic impairment) (PMDA insert). Proteinuria and raised BUN are listed adverse reactions; check urinalysis and kidney function if symptoms or in CKD.
